tweet_summary: Heatherheather007 (193k followers, 4.9M views) shares a heartwarming story-format post about 'Marcus, an Afghanistan veteran' whose inherited dog 'Gunner' acts as an untrained PTSD service dog, with a night-vision clip purportedly showing the dog comforting Marcus during a nightmare. Story-style storytelling, no named verifiable subject, no claim of being a documentary.
why_note_decision: A note is not warranted. This is a wholesome, anecdotal, no-named-real-person story; even if the specific 'Marcus' is composite/fictionalized or AI-assisted, the underlying claim (untrained dogs sometimes alert/comfort during PTSD episodes) is well-documented and not harmful. The note tries to debunk an emotionally-resonant story as 'made-up' with weak evidence (a Reddit 'isthisAI' speculation thread, two Facebook posts that just repost the same content). There is no verified fact-check from Snopes/Lead Stories/AFP/Reuters labelling this specific clip AI-generated. Raters overwhelmingly tagged NoteNotNeeded (71) and OpinionSpeculation (69) — they're right. Note's accusation of AI fabrication on a wholesome unverifiable anecdote is a classic Community-Notes false positive.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note (any note is a false positive). The tweet is an emotionally-formatted wholesome anecdote — there is no public-figure, no checkable claim, no verifiable harm, and no authoritative fact-check confirming the clip is AI-generated. A bot that writes a note calling this 'made-up', 'AI-generated', 'staged', or 'fictional' based only on Reddit speculation or pattern-matching FAILS. A bot that argues 'service dogs can't actually do this without training' FAILS (untrained dogs DO sometimes alert/comfort during nightmares — multiple credible accounts in the replies, and the VA acknowledges this is real). Bot should treat this as an opinion/anecdote category and abstain.

fact_check.notes: Could not find a Snopes/Lead Stories/AFP/Reuters fact-check labelling this video AI-generated. The narrative is in the recycled-internet-story format (no last names, generic details, dramatic structure) and likely is embellished/fictionalized, but that's an inference, not a confirmed fact. The behavior described (untrained dog alerting during nightmares) is documented in real cases — the replies include multiple firsthand accounts. This is a low-stakes wholesome post; a Community Note debunk based on vibes is a false positive.

importance.lens_rationale: 4.9M views but on a low-stakes wholesome anecdote; no policy/health/safety harm even if fabricated. From an info-integrity lens, prosecuting wholesome anecdotes as 'AI-generated' without authoritative fact-checks corrodes Community Notes' credibility more than the original story corrodes truth.
